race: Formula 1 MSC Cruises Grande Prêmio de São Paulo 2026

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Welcome to The Race Weekend Podcast, where Brazil rain, pole position, and penalties make Sunday feel like a live show you cannot look away from.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Norris took pole in a wet qualifying session delayed nearly an hour and a half by heavy rain at Interlagos, and it was a dramatic moment.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: That delay changed everything, because the track was still changing when the best car found the grip, and the whole grid had to guess.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: And the grid got messy, because Verstappen, Hamilton, and Leclerc all carry penalties into the start, so the first lap is a real battle.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Ferrari's Hamilton and Leclerc problem is real, but both can still be dangerous if the car is strong and the pit wall is brave.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Meanwhile, the boy from Bologna who became world champion says his title is the beginning of something special, and we agree.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Top three first. Kimi Antonelli is our one, because the champion has the best race pace and Mercedes love Interlagos in all conditions.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: He averages second here over one race, and that podium proves Mercedes can turn qualifying into a win without panic.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: The title win adds fuel, because he is not just fast, he is calm when the pressure is on and the cameras are close.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: But can Lando beat that from pole position when the track is slick, the mistakes are easy, and the rain is still moving?

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Lando starts from pole position, and his recent form says he wants the race, not just a podium, not just a photo.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: He averages third here over three races, with a best first and two podiums, so he is a proven Interlagos threat in any weather.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: I like his dry speed, but wet conditions can make him even more unpredictable on the front row, and that is fun.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: George Russell is our third, even though he has no podium here yet, and that is the whole story for Sunday.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: He starts second, has consistent Mercedes race pace, and his history is an average fourth over two races, so he is safe and sharp.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: So Mercedes own the front, but can they hold off a McLaren that starts from pole position and wants to strike at the right moment?

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Deep cut time. Lewis Hamilton is our eighth, not ninth, because Ferrari pace can erase a big grid penalty if he manages the first lap.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: That is a gamble, but the Ferrari car is strong and a wet start can shuffle everything into the right order for a surprise.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Hamilton can recover from the back, and a wet track rewards patience, especially when the spray is thick.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: I am buying it, because the grid hands him a problem, but the car hands him a chance to steal the race and make the headlines.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Now the low confidence gamble is Oliver Bearman in tenth, and he could be the name we remember if the front row fights.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: He starts eighth, has good recent points finishes, and Haas can be sneaky when the rain arrives and the big cars make mistakes.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: If the front row spins, Bearman is the name that jumps to the front of the conversation, and maybe the podium too.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Max Verstappen is fourth, because Red Bull pace and his Interlagos record can beat a grid penalty if he gets a clean start.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Charles Leclerc is fifth, because Ferrari pace and fourth place qualifying can carry him forward, and the car is strong.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Isack Hadjar is sixth, Liam Lawson is seventh, and Oscar Piastri is ninth, because all three have race pace and the confidence to use it.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Full top ten in one breath, Kimi Antonelli, Lando Norris, George Russell, Max Verstappen, Charles Leclerc, Isack Hadjar, Liam Lawson, Lewis Hamilton, Oscar Piastri, Oliver Bearman. Enjoy the race, follow the chaos, and we will be back with more.
